comments.author: apocryphox
comments.body_html:
Honestly, this is an absolute must-have mod for me.

I genuinely do not understand why, in vanilla SPT, 90% of the people from my own faction are friendly or neutral toward me. Even after spending quite a bit of time in EFT, around 50 to 100 hours total, which I know is not much for many people but still, I still have a hard time telling friend from foe. And for me, Tarkov is supposed to be difficult.

But what is the point of having a raid where mostly BEARs and Scavs are running around, and barely anyone shoots at me just because I also happen to be BEAR?

I see a PMC or a Scav, I can barely identify them visually with any certainty, so I shoot just to be safe. And if it turns out to be a BEAR, then he was basically a “free kill” because he would never have actively fought me anyway. That feels less like Tarkov and more like Arma.

Just because someone is BEAR does not automatically mean they are your friend. In a raid, the rule should be: your own squad is friendly, everyone else is potentially hostile.

Because of that, BEARs no longer become passive loot pinatas when you are playing as BEAR. They become actual PMC enemies. That makes Ground Zero and similar maps feel much more believable, because you can no longer walk through half the map full of same-faction PMCs who simply ignore you.

In a place like Tarkov, the idea of same faction=friend is questionable anyway. You are not fighting on a clean front line with radio coordination, clear identification, shared command, and strict rules of engagement. You are in a chaotic, cut-off zone full of small splinter groups, traitors, loot interests, and panic. In that kind of environment, “shoot first, ask questions later” feels very plausible.

I like to imagine it more like DayZ, or hardcore survival in general: you see someone, you do not know what they want, and in most cases, the first shot decides the encounter.

For SPT, this is much more believable to me than BEARs simply ignoring you until you shoot them.

The only thing that might be a bit exaggerated is that literally everyone shoots everyone on sight. But as a gameplay compromise, that is probably still much better than half the map being passive just because they are from the same faction.
